full_judgment: 17. He further submits that a registered deed has presumptive value of correctness and the Court below on due consideration, correct appreciation and threadbare discussion of evidence on record found that the plaintiff failed to prove his case by adducing any evidence and there is no misreading or non consideration any evidence on record and committed no error of law and, as such, the rule is liable to be discharged. In respect our apex court in a case reported in 12 MLR (AD) 149 = 12 BLC (AD) 99 it was held that, Evidence Act: section 114(e). Presumption of correctness of registered documents, Specific Relief Act: Section 12 Suit for mere declaration without seeking cancellation of the document to which the plaintiff is a party is not maintainable, Code of Civil Procedure: Order XLI, rule 23 Remand of suit cannot be granted as a matter of course, where the suit was disposed of on contest and there was no material issue left undecided, the suit cannot be remanded to the trial court for giving opportunity to the plaintiff to fill up lacuna. Where the plaintiff was alleged the executant of the disputed kabala deed which is not void ab initio but voidable the suit for mere declaration without seeking cancellation thereof was not maintainable. The impugned kabala deed which was duly registered has a presumption of correctness as provided under section 114(e) of the Evidence Act. The onus lies upon the plaintiff to prove that it was forged and fabricated.
